title: Abelian presheaf sheafification preserves the fibre at a site point
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the universe of values [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathbf{Set}$ be a functor such that its category of elements $\mathcal N_u$ is cofiltered: its objects are $(U,x)$ with $x\in u(U)$, and an arrow $(V,y)\to(U,x)$ is $h:V\to U$ with $u(h)(y)=x$. Assume that for every covering family $\{U_i\to U\}$ and $x\in u(U)$ there are $i$ and $y\in u(U_i)$ mapping to $x$. Thus $u$ defines a point of the site. For an abelian presheaf $P:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Ab}$ set $P_u=\varinjlim_{(U,x)\in\mathcal N_u^{\mathrm{op}}}P(U)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. If $\theta:P\to P^\#$ is abelian sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], the induced homomorphism $\theta_u:P_u\to(P^\#)_u$ is an isomorphism, natural in $P$. It sends the class of $s\in P(U)$ at $(U,x)$ to the class of $\theta_U(s)$ at $(U,x)$.
